subject: Urgent: websocket truncation and partial-payload timeouts impacting ACMEHealth teleprompter
messages:
From: Daniel Frye <daniel.frye@acmehealth.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@acmehealth.com
Date: Mon, 01 Jul 2028 09:12:45 -0700
Subject: Teleprompter feed: repeated truncation + timeouts (production)

Jasmine —

We started seeing degraded behavior on our teleprompter integration at ~08:45 PDT. The session initially streams tokens fine for ~10-30s, then the client sees repeated truncated frames (partial JSON chunks) and eventually a keepalive timeout after ~60s. Our logs show socket close with code 1006 and repeated 408-equivalent client errors. This is across several hosts in us-west-2.

Impact: presenters lose the live transcript and have to restart the feed — severe for today's clinical webinar.

Attached: a small trace (acme_ws_trace_20280701.json) and a short sample_chunk_log.txt.

Can you triage ASAP? We have a paid Dedicated subscription but are currently using the hosted endpoint.

—Daniel
Director, Platform Engineering
ACMEHealth

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Frye <daniel.frye@acmehealth.com>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 01 Jul 2028 09:18:02 -0700
Subject: Re: Teleprompter feed: repeated truncation + timeouts (production)

Dan — thanks for the heads up and for the traces. I'm escalating this to the on-call infra/streaming team.

Quick notes so you know what we'll try immediately:
- Flip the session to our short-poll fallback for >=30s sessions so presenters can continue while we investigate.
- Capture a live pcap on the edge for the next 30m (we'll coordinate a time).
- We'll also deploy an increased keepalive window at the edge (120s) as a stopgap.

David and Marissa — can you take point on this? Priorities: reproduce the partial-chunk condition, validate proxy backpressure counters, and confirm whether any autoscaler activity or kernel-level socket resets happened in the us-west-2 edge pool.

Dan — I'll update you within 20 minutes.

—Jasmine
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 01 Jul 2028 09:25:37 -0700
Subject: Re: Teleprompter feed: repeated truncation + timeouts (production)

Jasmine / Marissa — I'm seeing correlated alerts: p95 websocket chunk gap increased from ~40ms to 1.8s starting 08:43 PDT, and token emit error-rate jumped to 3.6% (baseline 0.02%). There were a series of proxy reset events with SYN_RECV spikes on the edge ingress proxies at 08:44:10–08:46:00.

Initial hypothesis: intermittent proxy file descriptor exhaustion + upstream ingress reconnect causing half-chunk writes (chunk-length header sent but body truncated). Also seeing a small surge in concurrent long-lived sessions (burst + backlog) — the autoscaler did not scale fast enough because the scaling window is 2m.

What I did:
- Enabled verbose chunk logging for the affected edge hosts.
- Increased keepalive to 120s on the affected host group.
- Triggered a manual pool scale of +20% (in progress).

Next steps: collect the edge verbose logs and a combined trace to correlate chunk boundary writes with proxy resets. Marissa — can you pull the scaled pool health and kernel logs (dmesg) for the timeframe?

—David
Senior SRE
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 01 Jul 2028 09:43:21 -0700
Subject: Re: Teleprompter feed: repeated truncation + timeouts (production)

Looping in Rishi given ACME's executive-level impact risk.

Findings so far:
- Edge host e-west-42 had 47k open file descriptors at peak; kernel reported "too many open files" warnings around 08:44:12.
- Proxy process (redwood-edge-proxy v2.12.0) restarted twice for oom_kill on worker threads (we're investigating the root cause).
- Autoscaler metrics: scaling decision lagged ~90s due to a combined spike from ACME and another large customer event.

Mitigations applied:
1) Manually recycled the proxy process and raised ulimit for the proxy user.
2) Temporarily moved ACME long-lived sessions to reserved warm pool (dedicated-like routing) to stabilize their sessions while we root cause.
3) Set server-side chunk guard to detect and repair half-chunk writes by re-requesting the last sequence if a header/body mismatch is seen (will be enabled as a 30m feature flag).

Customer-facing ask: Jasmine — please offer ACME the short-poll fallback and request they resume the session. Also propose a 10% credit for today's outage window and offer a follow-up technical postmortem.

Initial ETA for RCA: 48 hours.

—Marissa
Principal Infra Engineer (on-call)
Redwood Inference

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Frye <daniel.frye@acmehealth.com>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 01 Jul 2028 10:03:10 -0700
Subject: Re: Teleprompter feed: repeated truncation + timeouts (production)

Dan — quick update and actions you can take now:

What we changed (applied at ~09:50 PDT):
- Migrated your long-lived sessions to our reserved warm pool (routing change) — you should see substantially fewer truncations.
- Increased keepalive to 120s at the edge.
- Enabled short-poll fallback for any presenters who still experience issues (client change not required).

As a temporary relief, we can also flip your account to dedicated capacity for the rest of the week if you want — engineering will keep it pinned and monitor closely.

Apologies again for the disruption. We're initiating a post-incident review and will share the RCA and timeline for permanent fixes within 48 hours. For today, we will apply a one-time 10% service credit for the impacted session window; I'll confirm with finance and share a doc link.

Please let me know if you'd like us to keep the warm-pool routing or migrate to Dedicated for the rest of the day.

—Jasmine
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Daniel Frye <daniel.frye@acmehealth.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@acmehealth.com
Date: Mon, 01 Jul 2028 13:05:12 -0700

Thanks Jasmine — the warm-pool migration worked and the presenters completed the webinar with only one short restart. Appreciated the rapid fixes and the offer of a credit.

Please proceed with the warm-pool approach for the rest of today; we'd like to evaluate the RCA before moving to Dedicated. We'll expect the postmortem and a recommended fix list.

—Daniel

ACMEHealth
